title: Reverse Words With Same Vowel Count
summary: Given a string of lowercase English words separated by spaces, count the vowels in the first word.
statement: Given a string of lowercase English words separated by spaces, count the vowels in the first word. Reverse each subsequent word with the same vowel count, leaving others unchanged. Return the modified string.
constraints: s has up to 100,000 lowercase letters with single spaces between words.
Count vowels a, e, i, o, u in the first word.
Reverse each later word with that same count; never reverse the first word.
hints: The first word establishes one fixed target vowel count.
Scan each remaining word once and compare its vowel count with the target.
Reverse only matching later words, then join with single spaces.
Each word decision depends only on its own count and the unchanged first-word target.
editorial: Each word decision depends only on its own count and the unchanged first-word target.

tests.explanation: cat has one vowel, so and reverses to dna while mice remains unchanged.
book has two vowels; only nice matches and becomes ecin.
